title: SDK-style dispatch: Spotticus drives Claude Code in-process
description:
Second dispatch path alongside scripts/trigger_claude.sh: instead of shelling out to the CLI and trapping signals, Spotticus uses the Claude Agent SDK (claude-agent-sdk, query() + ClaudeAgentOptions) to run the worker in-process.

What the SDK buys us that the CLI wrapper cannot have:
- max_turns, a real turn ceiling. The CLI has no such flag, which is why the shell wrapper needs a wall-clock watchdog.
- A live message stream, so Spotticus can log what the worker is doing and stop it mid-run.
- In-process lock handling: claim/release via spotticus.locks directly, no PID trap dance.

comments.author: home
comments.text: SDK in-process dispatch landed on develop: scripts/trigger_claude_sdk.py + features/05_sdk_dispatch.feature (6 scenarios green). Three fixes were needed to make the spec pass: (1) the stub codexbar payload used a rateLimits array but the parser's claude branch reads usage.primary/secondary dicts; (2) read_lock was leaving an empty lockfile behind (fixed in spotticus/locks.py); (3) hold_lock SIGTERMs the trigger pid, so trigger_claude_sdk.py now catches SIGTERM and stops between messages instead of dying mid-stream. Still TODO: wire 05_sdk_dispatch into CI (it needs .venv/bin/spotticus, which CI doesn't have) and decide on the claude-sibling-wip-steps stash.
